title: Understanding pedagogical challenges faced by technology teachers in special needs classrooms
abstract: <jats:p>Teaching learners with special educational needs requires dynamic and adaptive pedagogical strategies that can lead to social development and academic success. This can be possible if teachers are assisted in mitigating the daily challenges of teaching such learners. This qualitative exploratory case study investigated the pedagogical challenges encountered by two Grade 9 Technology teachers in the Capricorn District of Limpopo Province. This study used Shulman’s Content and Pedagogical Knowledge framework to understand teachers’ challenges. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations; all collected data were analysed thematically. This study found that teachers experienced various challenges, including the emotional labour of teaching, burnout in the LSEN environment and the enactment of instructional knowledge. The study concluded that the sampled teachers displayed weaknesses in lesson planning, activating learners’ prior knowledge, diagnosing errors, achieving curriculum objectives and sustaining engagement. As a result, it was recommended that support through teacher assistants, creative differentiated strategies and enhanced digital-technology literacy to improve outcomes for learners with special needs was imminent.</jats:p>
venue: Journal of Education and Learning Technology

title: Integration of Biomechanics and Digital Technology: Using Kinovea for Motion Analysis and Learning for Beginner Athletes
abstract:
<jats:p>Background: The integration of biomechanics with digital motion-analysis technologies has introduced new approaches for examining movement efficiency, kinematic characteristics, and technical patterns in walking and running activities. Kinovea, as an accessible motion-analysis software, provides both visual and quantitative feedback. However, its application in supporting technique development among beginner athletes remains insufficiently explored.
Aim: This study aims to describe the use of Kinovea in biomechanics training and examine its contribution to the awareness of kinematic characteristics and movement techniques among beginner athletes.
Methods: A descriptive qualitative design involved 72 beginner athletes aged 18–25 years selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected over 16 weeks through interviews, field observations, and motion video recordings analyzed using Kinovea. Kinematic data focused on joint angles, stride behavior, and movement phases during walking, running, and the flight phase. Qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis with NVivo 12, while kinematic results were interpreted descriptively to identify performance patterns and areas for technical refinement.
Result: Kinematic analysis showed coordinated joint-angle patterns across all phases. Walking analysis identified arm swing angles of 50.9°–58.8° and leg separation angles of 64.3°–67.2°, indicating a stable gait rhythm. The running analysis revealed knee angles of 68.8°–69.8° and elbow angles of 87.6°–89.1°, indicating efficient propulsive mechanics. The flight phase demonstrated knee angles of 81.2°–87.8° and elbow angles of 80.4°–88.3°, suggesting effective momentum use and postural stability. These measurements supported stride-efficiency assessment and technique evaluation. Qualitative findings revealed that Kinovea enabled athletes to interpret movement phases and identify technical inefficiencies through slow-motion and frame-by-frame visualization.
Conclusion: Kinovea supports basic motion analysis by providing clear kinematic information and helping beginner athletes observe and refine their movement techniques. The findings also offer practical value for coaches by enabling more precise identification of inefficient patterns and guiding targeted corrections during early-stage training.</jats:p>
venue: Journal of Coaching and Sports Science

title: A Review of Phishing Detection Techniques Using Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing
abstract: <jats:p>The goal of phishing attacks, which rank high among cyber risks, is to steal sensitive information (such as login passwords, financial data, and more) from unsuspecting people and companies. Blacklist, whitelist, rule, heuristic, and signature-based detection methods are no longer suitable due to the rising sophistication of phishing schemes. As a result, ML, DL, and NLP are rapidly becoming into effective instruments for detecting both well-known and brand-new forms of phishing. Background on phishing assaults, old ways of detecting them, and recent advances in intelligent phishing detection are all included in this article. It delves into several machine learning algorithms such as decision tree, LSTM, ANN, CNN, and RNN, as well as deep learning models like KNN, NB, and SVM. Also, natural language processing methods including word embedding, sentiment analysis, text categorization, and tokenization are explored with the aim of detecting phishing material. Presenting a comprehensive, precise, and up-to-the-minute phishing detection system is the ultimate goal of this study, which focuses on machine learning frameworks, performance indicators, present obstacles, and future research directions.</jats:p>
venue: Journal of Global Research in Multidisciplinary Studies(JGRMS)
ai_summary: ML, DL, and NLP are rapidly becoming into effective instruments for detecting both well-known and brand-new forms of phishing .

title: HYBRID NETWORK INTRUSION DETECTION SYSTEM BASED ON SIGNATURE ANALYSIS AND MACHINE LEARNING METHODS
abstract: <jats:p>In the context of increasing complexity of modern network infrastructures and the growing number of cyberattacks, improving the effectiveness of intrusion detection systems is a highly relevant task. The aim of this work is to develop and investigate a hybrid approach to network attack detection based on a combination of signature-based analysis and intelligent machine learning methods.  The research methods include analysis of requirements for anomaly detection systems, comparative analysis of existing solutions, design of a hybrid system architecture, and experimental modeling using multiclass classification of network traffic. The results demonstrate that integrating a neural model with a traditional detection system improves attack detection coverage and reduces the number of false positives.  The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of deploying the proposed architecture in real corporate networks, while the theoretical significance consists in substantiating the effectiveness of a hybrid approach to traffic analysis. Future research directions include adaptive model training and expansion of the range of detectable attacks.</jats:p>

title: Cyber Defense Digital Twins: A Federated Learning and Zero-Trust AI Architecture for Autonomous Threat Prediction and Response
abstract: <jats:p>Modern enterprise networks operate under persistent threats that exploit cloud-native misconfigurations, identity sprawl, and API vulnerabilities at machine speed. Existing security operations center (SOC) architectures remain largely reactive, signature-dependent, and incapable of predicting multi-stage lateral movement. This paper proposes the Cognitive Cyber Defense Digital Twin (CCDT), a unified architecture integrating federated learning (FL), graph neural network (GNN)-based attack-path forecasting, adversarially hardened detection models, and autonomous Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR) with deception engineering. The CCDT constructs a continuously synchronized digital replica of organizational assets and employs reinforcement learning-based red agents to stress-test detection models. A federated intelligence mesh enables cross-organizational privacy-preserving gradient sharing. Experimental evaluations against CICIDS-2018 and LANL datasets demonstrate 52% faster attack-path detection, 41% reduction in false positive rate, and 60% reduction in mean-time-to-respond (MTTR) compared to traditional SOC baselines. Integrated Explainable AI (XAI) modules using SHAP values enable audit-ready compliance reporting. The CCDT represents a paradigm shift from reactive monitoring to predictive, autonomous, and privacy-preserving cyber defense for hybrid cloud environments.</jats:p>
venue: International Journal of Scientific Research in Computer Science, Engineering and Information Technology

title: Wearable sensing technologies and machine learning for fatigue assessment in sport horses.
abstract: Fatigue in sport horses is a multifactorial phenomenon that critically affects performance, injury risk, and welfare, yet its real-time, field-based assessment remains an unmet challenge. To synthesise evidence on the use of wearable sensors and machine learning for fatigue-related monitoring in sport horses and to identify priorities for future fatigue assessment. Scoping review. This scoping review was conducted in accordance with PRISMA-ScR guidelines. Publications from 2015 to 2026 were identified through Web of Science, Scopus, and ScienceDirect. Evidence from 102 publications was synthesised across five sensing modalities-heart rate (HR)/heart rate variability (HRV), thermometry, inertial measurement units (IMUs), surface electromyography (sEMG), and GPS-alongside machine learning applications for feature extraction, state classification, and risk modelling. Our synthesis reveals a fundamental disconnect: while each technology captures distinct physiological or biomechanical correlates of load, including autonomic response, thermoregulatory strain, gait stability, neuromuscular activation, and external workload, none provides a standalone signature of fatigue. Only a minority of studies used fatigue as a direct modelling label, with most relying on proxy outcomes such as asymmetry or performance decrement. The included literature was heterogeneous in sensor modalities, study designs, outcome measures, and application contexts. In addition, the limited use of directly defined fatigue outcomes restricted comparison across studies and constrained conclusions regarding fatigue-specific monitoring. The path forward lies not in developing yet another single-sensor solution, but in establishing a multidimensional, context-aware framework that integrates complementary data streams, individualised baselines, and interpretable models. Future research should prioritise: (1) operationalised fatigue definitions; (2) longitudinal, within-horse monitoring designs; (3) robust multimodal fusion architectures; (4) rigorous external validation across equestrian disciplines; and (5) explainable artificial intelligence to bridge the gap between algorithmic output and actionable training decisions.

title: Artificial Intelligence as a Catalyst for Value-Based Care in Vascular Disease.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is increasingly used in vascular imaging, risk prediction, clinical text analysis, workflow coordination, and procedural planning, but its value depends on whether it turns available data into appropriate action and better outcomes at acceptable cost. In this structured narrative review of literature and regulatory sources through September 2026, we summarize a practical AI toolkit for vascular care in 5 categories: imaging, surveillance, procedural planning, workflow management, and decision support. Several tools are cleared by the U.S. Food and Drug Administration, mostly for aortic measurement, triage, and procedural guidance, but evidence remains largely retrospective and technical, with few studies of clinical action, outcomes, cost, or equity. We propose a value-based framework that evaluates AI across 5 steps (data, detection, context, action, and outcome) and offer practical questions to guide adoption. In conclusion, the value of vascular AI depends on whether it improves care and patient outcomes across complete clinical pathways, with attention to resource use, safety, and equity.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Behavioral Phenotyping: From Behavioral Neuroscience to Depression Research.
abstract: Behavioral phenotyping remains the main experimental readout for investigating brain function and neuropsychiatric disease. However, conventional behavioral analysis relies largely on manually defined endpoints that simplify the multidimensional nature of behavior and often overlook subtle behavioral dynamics. Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI), particularly machine learning (ML), deep learning (DL) and computer vision, are fundamentally transforming this landscape by enabling automated, high-resolution quantification of behavior across species and experimental paradigms. This review discusses recent developments in AI-based behavioral phenotyping and their implications for translational neuroscience, with particular emphasis on emerging applications to depression research. We first describe how markerless pose estimation has changed movement quantification, followed by supervised and unsupervised ML approaches that classify predefined behaviors or discover latent behavioral motifs directly from movement data. We then discuss how these approaches are reshaping systems neuroscience by enabling increasingly detailed descriptions of behavioral organization and facilitating the investigation of behavior as a continuous, multidimensional process. Finally, we examine their application to experimental models and clinical studies of depression, considering their potential and the limitations of translating computational behavioral measures across experimental and clinical settings. AI-based behavioral phenotyping represents an important methodological advance in neuroscience, shifting behavioral analysis from the quantification of isolated experimental endpoints toward the characterization of integrated behavioral states. In depression research, these approaches may improve behavioral characterization in experimental models and provide quantitative measures of clinically-relevant behavioral alterations in humans. However, linking experimental and clinical phenotypes will require methodological standardization, independent validation, and careful evaluation of cross-species comparability.
venue: Neuroscience and biobehavioral reviews

title: Foundation models in radiology: Development, applications, and future impact.
abstract: Foundation models represent a major evolution in artificial intelligence, enabling models pretrained on large, diverse datasets to be adapted to a wide range of downstream tasks with substantially less task-specific training data. In radiology, advances in transformer architectures, self-supervised learning, and vision-language models have created new opportunities to integrate image and text understanding within versatile artificial intelligence systems. Potential applications span the radiology workflow and include image interpretation, automated report drafting and summarization, clinical decision support, information retrieval, and development of specialized task-specific models. Among these, AI-assisted report generation represents a particularly promising near-term application, although current performance supports a role as a drafting assistant rather than an autonomous replacement for radiologists. Important barriers to clinical adoption remain, including limitations in model performance, regulatory requirements, and the risk of automation bias. In the near term, foundation models may have their greatest impact by augmenting radiologists and accelerating the development of specialized artificial intelligence applications rather than replacing existing systems or physician expertise. This review describes the technological advances underlying foundation models, highlights their current and emerging applications in radiology, examines key risks and implementation challenges, and considers their potential impact on the future practice of radiology.

title: [A review of endoscopic embodied intelligence: current status and prospects].
abstract: 消化内镜具身智能是融合机器人学、人工智能与临床医学的前沿交叉领域，旨在推动内镜诊疗由人工操作向自动化与智能化迈进。本文按照“感知-决策-执行”框架，系统梳理该领域的研究现状、核心挑战与发展前景。按系统组成将其归纳为“内镜之手”（执行器）、“内镜之眼”（感知器）与“内镜之脑”（决策器）三个层面：“内镜之手”涵盖检查机器人与治疗机器人，总结从诊断到治疗的分级机器人化路径；“内镜之眼”从视觉感知与辅助感知两个维度，归纳当前内镜具身智能的信息感知研究；“内镜之脑”将智能方法概括为辨识智能与行为智能，梳理其在病变识别、腔内导航及手术辅助中的进展。在此基础上，对消化内镜具身智能的当前发展阶段和面对挑战进行总结，并对未来研究方向做出展望：应加强机器人本体与多模态感知的深度集成，研发面向临床、决策透明可靠的具身智能模型，同时推动与之相适应的新型医疗监管体系的建立，以构建安全、可信、高效的具身智能内镜诊疗体系。.

title: [Expert consensus on artificial intelligence optical navigation-assisted CT-guided percutaneous for thoracic lesions].
abstract: Conventional CT-guided percutaneous for thoracic lesions is primarily performed via freehand manipulation by the operator, and its accuracy is constrained by individual experience. Artificial intelligence optical navigation-assisted systems enable precise execution of preplanned puncture trajectories and visual guidance through high-precision spatial localization and robotic arm navigation, thereby markedly improving puncture success rate and procedural safety. To standardize and promote this technique and advance the precision diagnosis and treatment of thoracic tumors, this consensus was formulated by domestic experts organized jointly by the Ablation Expert Committee of the Chinese Society of Clinical Oncology (CSCO), the Society of Tumor Ablation Therapy of the Chinese Anti-Cancer Association, the Expert Group on Tumor Ablation Therapy of the Chinese Medical Doctors Association, the Tumor Ablation Committee of the Chinese College of Interventionalists,following in-depth discussions. This consensus mainly covers: (1) artificial intelligence optical navigation systems and puncture devices; (2) protocols and precautions for artificial intelligence optical navigation-assisted CT-guided percutaneous puncture for thoracic lesions. 传统CT引导经皮胸部病变穿刺主要依赖术者徒手操作，其精准度受限于个人经验。人工智能光学导航辅助系统通过高精度空间定位与机械臂导航，能够精准执行预设穿刺路径及提供可视化引导，从而显著提升穿刺成功率与操作安全性。为规范并推广该项技术，推动胸部肿瘤精准诊疗的发展，由中国临床肿瘤学会（CSCO）肿瘤消融治疗专家委员会、中国抗癌协会肿瘤消融治疗专业委员会、中国医师协会肿瘤消融治疗技术专家组及中国医师协会介入医师分会肿瘤消融专家工作组共同组织国内相关专家，经充分讨论后制订本共识。共识主要内容涵盖：（1）人工智能光学导航设备及穿刺器械；（2）人工智能光学导航辅助CT引导经皮胸部病变穿刺的操作规程与注意事项。.

title: [Application progress and challenges of artificial intelligence in the smart transformation of infectious disease hospitals].
abstract: ​ Artificial intelligence (AI) is changing the way infectious disease hospitals operate, expanding their role beyond patient care to include surveillance and early warning, public health coordination, and research translation. This review summarizes the major applications of AI in intelligent surveillance and early warning, clinical care, infection prevention and control, and intelligent hospital operations management. Considering business needs, technological maturity, and implementation risks, we discuss the appropriate implementation priorities, requirements, and evaluation approaches for different application scenarios. We further propose a framework for intelligent transformation that is built on data interoperability, prioritizes high-value application scenarios, and is supported by stratified implementation and lifecycle governance, with the aim of providing a practical reference for the development and evaluation of AI applications in infectious disease hospitals. 人工智能（AI）正在改变传染病医院的工作方式，使其不再只是患者救治终端，也参与监测预警、公共卫生协同和科研转化。本文梳理了AI在智能监测预警、临床诊疗、院感防控和智能化运行管理中的主要应用，并结合业务需求、技术成熟度和实施风险，讨论不同场景的建设顺序、落地条件和评价方法，并提出了以数据互通为基础、以高价值业务场景为重点、以分层应用和全生命周期治理为保障的智慧化转型思路，为传染病医院相关建设和应用评价提供支撑。.

title: Cold-Shock-Primed Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG Extracellular Vesicles Restore Liver-Gut Axis Homeostasis Through Bile Acid Metabolic Reprogramming in MASLD.
abstract: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is intricately linked to gut-liver axis dysfunction, wherein microbial dysbiosis, bile acid dysregulation, and impaired intestinal barrier function synergistically drive disease pathogenesis. Here, we developed a nanotherapeutic platform using Lactobacillus rhamnosus GG-derived extracellular vesicles (LGG-EVs). Cold-shock fermentation (28°C) doubled the EV yield without compromising bioactivity. Following intraperitoneal administration in high-fat diet (HFD)-induced MASLD mice, LGG-EVs preferentially accumulated in the liver, where they reestablished bile acid homeostasis through Pparα-mediated reprogramming of Cyp7a1 and Cyp7b1 expression, reduced hepatic steatosis by suppressing lipogenic gene programs, and attenuated inflammation via inhibition of NF-κB/MAPK signalling. This hepatic bile acid modulation subsequently alleviated intestinal bile acid accumulation, restored intestinal barrier integrity via upregulation of tight-junction proteins, and reduced intestinal permeability. These intestinal improvements were accompanied by restoration of gut microbiota composition, marked by enrichment of beneficial taxa such as Akkermansia, Muribaculaceae, and Lachnospiraceae_NK4A136, alongside reduction in the Firmicutes/Bacteroidota ratio. Collectively, by orchestrating bidirectional liver-gut axis repair-initiated by hepatic bile acid metabolic reprogramming and propagated through gut microbiota restoration and intestinal barrier reinforcement-cold-shock-enhanced LGG-EVs represent a safe, high-yield nanomedicine for MASLD therapy.
